content.text:
I submitted index 27 (Cr 0.156 / Sb 0.844) as the best composition. Its EQE of 0.076% was the highest of the three measurements, and I used the full merit budget of 3.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 18 | 0.634 | 0.041 |
| 25 | 0.818 | 0.063 |
| 27 | 0.844 | **0.076** |

- **Trend:** EQE went up with Sb content at every step. Index 27 is the most Sb-rich film in the library and it was still rising there, so I can't tell whether the best composition is index 27 or one I didn't measure.
- **Coverage:** I only measured the Sb-rich half. Everything below Sb 0.63 (indices 0–17) was left out, based on one XRD scan and the trend from these three points.
- **XRD:** I used 3 of the 5 scans. The strongest peak in every scan (Q ≈ 5.33) is probably from the substrate, not the film. Beyond that, the Sb-rich films (indices 18 and 25) show a clean rutile pattern, and the Cr-rich film (index 10) has extra peaks that suggest a second phase. That film had no EQE measurement.
- **Model predictions:** These were weak evidence. Rutile CrSbO₄ is predicted to have a band gap of about 1.7–2.0 eV, so it should absorb the 3.2 eV light. The Sb-rich structures are predicted to be only slightly unstable (about 0.1 eV/atom), which fits them staying rutile. None of this picked out a best composition.
